caveat: One repository, and the only one measured with a build declaration this module can read. The automake and CMake readers are first cuts; a project using bazel, meson or setuptools declares nothing to them yet and is correctly left alone rather than guessed at.

delta.entailed_findings: 0 -> 3, and all three are false positives -- see below
delta.interprocedural_regions: 25 -> 1 (the survivor is contrib/tools/pngfix.c:main, which bin_PROGRAMS installs)

how.not_shipped_is_not_unscanned: Non-shipped regions are still arbitrated, function-locally. A contributor editing a test must still get an answer about it; what they lose is the expensive interprocedural treatment and first claim on the budget.
how.silence_is_not_exclusion: A repository with no build file this can read gets None back and nothing changes. vampi declares nothing, so its numbers are untouched.
how.the_project_declares_it: Makefile.am names installed targets in lib_LTLIBRARIES and bin_PROGRAMS, and each target's <target>_SOURCES names its files. check_PROGRAMS and noinst_PROGRAMS are automake's own word for 'not installed', which is exactly the distinction wanted. Taking every _SOURCES would have called libpng's whole test suite shipped code -- contrib/libtests declares its sources the same way the library does.

reading: A project's own build files say what it ships, and libpng's say the library plus two installed tools. Every one of its twenty-five entry-point regions was a main() in an example program or a test tool, and those regions carried the interprocedural analysis that dominated the query phase. Ranking build-declared code first and withholding the interprocedural treatment from the rest cuts the taint query by 58% and changes no region count: not shipped is not unscanned.

the_three_new_findings_are_false_positiv.structural_cause: Both C families carry ZERO sanitizers: c/injection and c/memory each have 0. No C flow can ever be discharged, and there is no notion of a bounds guard at all -- so every argv -> strcpy in any C codebase entails, however carefully it is bounded. Guard dominance is exactly the abstraction that decides this, and it is wired to access_control only. Recorded as task 2.12.
the_three_new_findings_are_false_positiv.why_it_is_safe: outname is char[256], and line 325 guards with `if ((len = strlen(inname)) > 250)`. By line 374 len <= 250, so the copy writes at most 255 bytes. The bound dominates the sink.
the_three_new_findings_are_false_positiv.why_they_appeared_now: They were not introduced by this change so much as uncovered by it: with callDepth 3 the sink set was different, and the 26 fgets false positives were masking them. Three identical rows for one site is task 2.9 again.
